title: Judy's Magic cast-on
subtitle: The two-circular cast-on for working toe-up from the very tip.
excerpt: Judy's Magic cast-on starts a flat oval of live stitches on two needle tips, giving a closed toe for top-down socks or the tip of a mitten. No grafting or seaming needed at the start.
sourceNotes: Technique popularised in modern sock-knitting community from traditional central-start methods. Structurally related to the Turkish cast-on and to Beeton's method for starting knitted lace from the centre (Beeton's Book of Needlework, 1870). Yarn-around-needle mechanics described in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938).

glossaryTerms.definition: A cast-on method that distributes stitches over two needle tips simultaneously, producing a closed oval of live stitches for working a flat toe or central-start piece in the round.

content.text: (named for knitter and designer Judy Becker, who published it in the early 2000s) places stitches on two needle tips at once by wrapping the yarn in alternating directions. When you work the first round, the needle tips part and the piece opens into a flat oval. It is the standard start for a toe-up sock: no seam to graft, no provisional yarn to pull out. Difficulty: advanced, because the two-needle setup takes practice to hold in the first few wraps.
Two circular needles of the same size (or one long circular for magic loop)
Patience for the first two wraps
Hold both needle tips parallel in the right hand, tips pointing left. Drape the yarn over both needles so the tail falls between the needles and the working end hangs behind the lower needle.
Holding the yarn ends in the left hand, wrap the tail over the top needle from below and bring it back between the needles. This places one stitch on the top needle.
Wrap the working yarn under the bottom needle from above and bring it back between the needles. This places one stitch on the bottom needle.
Alternate steps 2 and 3 until you have the required number of stitches on each needle. The cast-on number should be half the total toe stitches you need.

To work the first round, knit across the top needle stitches. When you reach the bottom needle, the stitches sit with their leading legs on the back of the needle. Knit each one through the back loop to untwist it.
After the first round, work normally. The oval will be clear from round two onward.

Toe-up sock patterns almost universally use Judy's Magic cast-on or the Turkish cast-on, which is structurally similar. It also starts fingerless mitts where the thumb is at the top, and some square shawl patterns that build outward from the centre.

items.symptom: First round produces twisted stitches on one needle
items.cause: The bottom-needle stitches sit twisted by design; top-needle stitches should not be twisted
items.fix: Only knit the bottom-needle stitches through the back loop. Work the top-needle stitches normally. If both sets are twisted, the wrapping direction was reversed.

items.symptom: Yarn tail too short to complete the cast-on
items.fix: Pull out at least 40 cm of tail before starting. The two-strand wrapping method uses more tail than a single-strand cast-on.

items.symptom: First round is extremely difficult to work
items.cause: Stitches wound too tightly onto the needles
items.fix: Keep wraps relaxed. A cast-on that is slightly loose is far easier to work into and will tighten up as the first round progresses.
